facts.statement: Fossils of Kentisuchus have been found in England and France dating to the early Eocene.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from England and France that date back to the early Eocene.

facts.statement: Kentisuchus has been recorded from Ukraine, though it is unclear if those specimens belong to the genus.
facts.quote: The genus has also been recorded from Ukraine, but it unclear whether specimens from Ukraine are referable to Kentisuchus.

facts.statement: William Buckland named Crocodylus spenceri based on a partial skull found on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, England.
facts.quote: William Buckland named "Crocodylus" spenceri on the basis of a partial skull found from the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, England.

facts.statement: Charles Mook erected the genus Kentisuchus in 1955 for the species originally described by Richard Owen in 1849.
facts.quote: The genus Kentisuchus was erected by Charles Mook in 1955 for the species "Crocodylus" toliapicus, described by Richard Owen, in 1849.

facts.statement: Recent molecular studies indicate that Tomistominae, including extinct forms like Kentisuchus, belong to Gavialoidea and Gavialidae rather than being crocodiles.
facts.quote: recent molecular studies using DNA sequencing have consistently indicated that the false gharial (Tomistoma) (and by inference other related extinct forms in Tomistominae) actually belong to Gavialoidea (and Gavialidae).

facts.statement: Research suggests Kentisuchus dispersed from mainland Europe to islands in the Tethysian archipelago rather than migrating from Africa.
facts.quote: The close relation of Kentisuchus and Dollosuchoides, which are known from European localities that were on the mainland during the early Eocene, to Megadontosuchus, which is known from Italian localities that were once part of a Tethysian archipelago, suggests that it came to these islands after a dispersal event south from mainland Europe rather than north from Africa.

facts.statement: Kentisuchus lived between 56 and 37.71 million years ago during the Ypresian to Bartonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Bartonian (56 to 37.71 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kentisuchus is classified under the parent group Gavialoidea.

rejected.statement: Kentisuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodylian that was traditionally classified within the subfamily Tomistominae.
rejected.quote: Kentisuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodylian, traditionally regarded as a member of the subfamily Tomistominae.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Kentisuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodylian'
